content: The United States Navy ship USS Canberra (LCS-30) arrived at the Port of Colombo this morning, 26 October 2026 for replenishment purposes. The visiting ship was welcomed by the Sri Lanka Navy in accordance with naval traditions. This 127.6 metre long Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) is commanded by Commander C Towles. Commissioned on 22 July 2023, USS Canberra (LCS-30) has since been in service with the US Navy. The ship previously made a port call in Sri Lanka on 12 June this year.

summary_en: 2026 වසරේ මුල් මාස නවය තුළ ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ සමස්ත අපනයන ආදායම ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 13.61 සීමාව දක්වා ළඟා වී ඇති අතර එය 2025 අනුරූප කාලපරිච්ඡේදයේ වාර්තා වූ ඇමරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 12.96 ට සාපේක්ෂව 5.04% ක ඉහළ යාමකි. මෙම ධනාත්මක කාර්ය සාධනය සදහා වෙළඳ භාණ්ඩ සහ සේවා අපනයන යන අංශ දෙකෙහිම වර්ධනය සහාය වී ඇත. ශ්‍රී ලංකා රේගුව විසින් නිකුත් කරන ලද නවතම අපනයන කාර්යසාධන දත්තවලට අනුව සහ මැණික් හා ස්වර්ණාභරණ මෙන්ම ඛනිජ තෙල් නිෂ්පාදන අපනයනය සම්බන්ධයෙන් ශ්‍රී ලංකා අපනයන සංවර්ධන මණ්ඩලය (EDB) විසින් ඉදිරිපත් කරන ලද ඇස්තමේන්තුවලට අනුව , 2026 ජනවාරි සිට සැප්තැම්බර් දක්වා කාලය තුළ ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ භාණ්ඩ අපනයන ආදායම 5.35% කින් වර්ධනය වී ඇත. එය ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 10.76 කි. 2025 වසරේ මෙම කාලසීමාව තුළ වාර්තා වූ භාණ්ඩ අපනයන ආදායම ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 10.22 ක් වූ අතර , ඒ අනුව මෙම වසරේ මුල් මාස නවය තුළ භාණ්ඩ අපනයන ආදායමේ සැලකිය යුතු වර්ධනයක් පෙන්නුම් කරයි. 2025 වසරේ මෙම කාලසීමාව තුළ ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 2.74 ක් ලෙස වාර්තා වූ සේවා අපනයන ආදායම , 2026 ජනවාරි සිට සැප්තැම්බර් දක්වා කාලය තුළ 3.88% කින් වර්ධනය වී ඇත. එය ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 2.85 කි. මෙම සාධනීය වර්ධනය 2026 සැප්තැම්බර් මාසයේ කාර්යසාධනය තුළ ද පිළිඹිබු වූ අතර , එහිදී සමස්ත අපනයන ආදායම ඇමෙරිකානු ඩොලර් බිලියන 1.6 9 ක් දක්වා ළඟා වූ අතර, එය 2025 සැප්තැම්

content:
Grammy-winning singer Chris Brown is to be sentenced Monday over brawling at a London nightclub three years ago.

Brown, 37, pleaded guilty to a count of affray at London’s Southwark Crown Court in July for attacking a music producer with a bottle on the head.

Brown had denied attacking Abraham Diaw with a bottle at the Tape nightclub in the swanky Mayfair neighborhood in February 2023. But prosecutors said the fight was caught on surveillance camera in front of a club full of people.

In return for the guilty plea, prosecutors dropped charges of assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and having an offensive weapon, a bottle.

Brown's friend and vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu also pleaded guilty to affray. He will be sentenced too.

Brown left the United Kingdom after the brawl but was arrested in May 2025 at a Manchester hotel after flying to the city for a concert.

Brown had been free on bail of 5 million pounds ($6.7 million), which allowed him to tour Europe and North America last summer. He was freed on bail again Friday and will be sentenced Oct. 26 on the affray charge, which carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison.

Brown, who rose to stardom as a teen in 2005, won his first Grammy for best R&B album in 2011 for “F.A.M.E.” He earned his second in the same category for “11:11 (Deluxe)” in 2025.

He has been in repeated legal trouble since his felony conviction in the 2009 assault of his then-girlfriend, Rihanna, hours before the pair were due to perform at the Grammys.

He has been arrested in several U.S. states over altercations, and in 2019 he was arrested in Paris and questioned on suspicion of rape. He was released without charge.

Brown had denied attacking Abraham Diaw with a bottle at the Tape nightclub in the swanky Mayfair neighborhood in February 2023. But prosecutors said the fight was caught on surveillance camera in front of a club full of people.

In return for the guilty plea, prosecutors dropped charges of assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and having an offensive weapon, a bottle.

Brown's friend and vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu also pleaded guilty to affray. He will be sentenced too.

Brown left the United Kingdom after the brawl but was arrested in May 2025 at a Manchester hotel after flying to the city for a concert.

Brown had been free on bail of 5 million pounds ($6.7 million), which allowed him to tour Europe and North America last summer. He was freed on bail again Friday and will be sentenced Oct. 26 on the affray charge, which carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison.

Brown, who rose to stardom as a teen in 2005, won his first Grammy for best R&B album in 2011 for “F.A.M.E.” He earned his second in the same category for “11:11 (Deluxe)” in 2025.

He has been in repeated legal trouble since his felony conviction in the 2009 assault of his then-girlfriend, Rihanna, hours before the pair were due to perform at the Grammys.

He has been arrested in several U.S. states over altercations, and in 2019 he was arrested in Paris and questioned on suspicion of rape. He was released without charge.

content: Sri Lanka’s total exports have reached US$ 13.61 Bn during the first nine months of 2026, recording a year-on-year growth of 5.04% compared with US$ 12.96 Bn in the corresponding period of 2025. This positive performance reflects the continued expansion of the country’s export sector, supported by growth in both merchandise and services exports. According to the latest export performance figures released by Sri Lanka Customs, together with the EDB’s estimates for gems and jewellery and petroleum products, merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$ 10.76 Bn during January–September 2026, compared with US$ 10.22 Bn recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Meanwhile, services exports grew by 3.88% to US$ 2.85 Bn, up from US$ 2.74 Bn in the corresponding period of the previous year. The performance of both segments highlights the importance of strengthening Sri Lanka’s export competitiveness while diversifying its sources of export earnings. Strong Export Performance in September 2026 Sri Lanka recorded a particularly strong performance in September 2026, with total exports reaching US$ 1.69 Bn, an impressive year-on-year increase of 17.23% compared with US$ 1.44 Bn in September 2025. Merchandise exports were the main driver of this monthly growth, increasing by 21.66% to US$ 1.39 Bn, compared with US$ 1.14 Bn in September 2025. Services exports also recorded a positive performance, rising by 0.67% to US$ 306.17 Mn from US$ 304.14 Mn in the corresponding month last year. The strong growth in merchandise exports during September contributed significantly to the overall improvement in export earnings, reinforcing the positive trajectory of Sri Lanka’s export sector. Sustaining Export Growth Towards National Targets The export performance achieved during the first nine months of 2026 represents continued progress towards strengthening Sri Lanka’s position in international markets and expanding its contribution to the national economy. Sustaining this momentum will require continued efforts to diversify export products and markets, enhance value addition, improve product quality and standards, and strengthen the competitiveness of Sri Lankan exporters. The National Export Development Plan (NEDP) 2026–2030, which targets US$ 36 Bn in annual export earnings by 2030, provides a strategic framework for accelerating export growth through improved trade facilitation, market development, investment promotion, innovation, and enhanced private-sector engagement. Building on the positive results recorded in the first nine months of 2026, continued coordination among government institutions, industry stakeholders, and exporters will be essential to maintaining growth, addressing emerging challenges, and realising Sri Lanka’s long-term export development ambitions. Commenting on the export performance in September 2026, Mr.Mangala Wijesinghe, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB), stated: “Sri Lanka’s total exports reaching US$ 13.61 Bn during the first nine months of 2026, representing a growth of 5.04% compared with the corresponding period of 2025, reflects the continued resilience and progress of our export sector. Particularly encouraging is the strong performance recorded in September, when total exports increased by 17.23% year-on-year to US$ 1.69 Bn, driven by a significant 21.66% growth in merchandise exports. This performance demonstrates the potential of Sri Lankan exporters to strengthen their presence in international markets despite an increasingly competitive global trading environment. As we move forward, our priority must be to sustain this growth momentum by strengthening the competitiveness of existing export sectors while accelerating the development of new products, services and markets. Enhancing value addition, promoting innovation and technology adoption, diversifying export markets, and integrating more deeply into global value chains will be essential to expanding export earnings and generating greater economic value for the country. The EDB remains committed to working closely with exporters, industry associations and relevant government institutions to address emerging challenges, improve the trade and investment environment, and facilitate greater access to international markets. Through the effective implementation of the National Export Development Plan 2026–2030 and strengthened collaboration among all stakeholders, we aim to build on these positive results, achieve sustainable export growth, and advance Sri Lanka towards its long-term ambition of reaching US$ 36 Bn in annual export earnings by 2030.” Major Exports in September 2026 Products and Services with Positive Growth (Increases) In September 2026, exports of Apparel and Textiles increased by 3.46%, reaching US$ 439.78 Mn compared with US$ 425.07 Mn in September 2025. Apparel exports grew by 3.43% to US$ 408.69 Mn, while textile exports increased by 3.81% to US$ 31.09 Mn. This positive year-on-year growth reflects the resilience of Sri Lanka’s apparel industry amid evolving global market conditions. Exports to the United States, a key destination for Sri Lankan apparel, also increased by 6.33%, contributing positively to the sector’s monthly performance. Rubber and Rubber-Based Products recorded a strong performance in September 2026, with export earnings increasing by 33.68% year-on-year to US$ 99.31 Mn, compared with US$ 74.29 Mn in September 2025. This growth was supported by improved performance across key product segments. Exports of Industrial and Surgical Rubber Gloves increased by 34.38% to US$ 31.70 Mn, while exports of Pneumatic and Retreaded Tyres and Tubes rose by 39.57% to US$ 54.95 Mn. These gains highlight the continued international demand for Sri Lankan rubber-based products and the sector’s competitiveness in global markets. Exports of Spices, Essential Oils and Oleoresins increased significantly by 73.19% in September 2026, reaching US$ 74.73 Mn compared with US$ 43.15 Mn in September 2025. Pepper exports surged by 165.38% to US$ 23.46 Mn, while cinnamon exports increased by 68.27% to US$ 42.59 Mn. Coconut Fibre-based Products also recorded a positive performance, with export earnings increasing by 2.99 % year-on-year. Activated Carbon, a high-value, value-added product derived from coconut shells, recorded a 43.52% year-on-year increase, with export earnings reaching US$ 25.26 Mn in September 2026. This strong performance underscores the growing contribution of diversified, value-added coconut-based products to Sri Lanka’s export earnings, while highlighting the sector’s potential for further value addition, product diversification and expansion in global markets. The Food and Beverages sector recorded a strong year-on-year increase of 27.92% in export earnings, reaching US$ 63.77 Mn in September 2026 compared with US$ 49.85 Mn in September 2025. This positive performance highlights the continued demand for Sri Lankan food and beverage products in international markets and the sector’s potential to further strengthen its contribution to the country’s export earnings. The Electrical and Electronic Components sector recorded significant growth of 88.35% in September 2026, with export earnings reaching US$ 68.54 Mn, compared to the corresponding month of 2025. This notable performance was mainly supported by a 114.62% increase in exports of Insulated Wires and Cables, highlighting Sri Lanka’s expanding participation in global value chains and supply networks. Seafood exports recorded a growth of 4.01% in September 2026, reaching US$ 23.61 Mn compared with US$ 22.7 Mn in September 2025. Frozen fish exports increased by 15.85% to US$ 13.96 Mn, while exports of shrimps rose by 207.27% to US$ 3.38 Mn. On the services export front, Transport and Logistics Services exports are estimated to have reached US$ 167.9 Mn in September 2026, reflecting a 23.32 % year-on-year increase compared with US$ 136.15 Mn in September 2025. This strong growth highlights the sector’s contribution to Sri Lanka’s services export performance and reinforces the country’s potential to strengthen its position as a competitive regional hub for transport, logistics and maritime services in global markets. Products with Negative Growth (Decreases) Tea export earnings declined by 1.38% year-on-year to US$ 135.11 Mn in September 2026, compared with US$ 137.0 Mn in September 2025. The decline was primarily attributable to weaker export performance in key markets, particularly the Middle East, where tea exports decreased by 26.85 % compared to September 2025. Within the region, exports to the United Arab Emirates, Iran, and Iraq recorded notable declines of 42.56%, 34.57%, and 55.73%, respectively, reflecting challenging market conditions affecting Sri Lanka’s tea exports. The Coconut-based Products sector recorded an 8.88% year-on-year decline in export earnings, falling to US$ 111.60 Mn in September 2026 from US$ 122.47 Mn in September 2025. Among the three major sub-categories, Coconut Kernel Products recorded the significant decline, decreasing by 29.15%. Within this category, export earnings from Coconut Oil and Liquid Coconut Milk declined by 19.25% and 26.89%, respectively, contributing significantly to the sector’s overall decline. Meanwhile, exports of Coco Peat, Fibre Pith and Moulded Products decreased by 10.63%, reaching US$ 21.44 Mn in September 2026. Ornamental fish exports declined by 35.15% year-on-year to US$ 1.55 Mn in September 2026, compared with US$ 2.39 Mn in September 2025. This substantial contraction highlights the challenges facing the sector’s monthly export performance. Exports of Non-metallic Mineral Products declined by 3.85% in September 2026 to US$ 10.24 Mn, compared with US$ 10.65 Mn in September 2025. Exports during the period of January – September 2026 Sri Lanka’s export performance remained positive during the January–September 2026 period, with total exports reaching an estimated US$ 13,612.55 Mn, reflecting a 5.04% year-on-year increase compared with US$ 12,959.17 Mn in the corresponding period of 2025. Merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$ 10,761.92 Mn, while services exports increased by 3.88% to US$ 2,850.63 Mn. The continued expansion of both merchandise and services exports highlights the resilience of Sri Lanka’s export sector amid evolving global market conditions. While merchandise exports remained the main contributor to overall export growth, the continued increase in services exports underscores their growing role in diversifying the export base and generating foreign exchange earnings. Sustaining this positive momentum will require strengthening export competitiveness, expanding access to international markets, promoting value-added products and services, and broadening the range of export sectors contributing to national economic growth. Products & Services with Positive Growth (Increases) Cumulative export earnings from several key sectors recorded strong growth during January–September 2026. Rubber-based Products, Coconut-based Products, Processed Food & Beverages, Electrical & Electronic Components, and Spices and Concentrates recorded year-on-year increases of 8.44%, 3.68%, 20.9%, 61.05 and 30.53% respectively. These gains highlight the growing contribution of value-added manufacturing and the continued potential for product diversification to strengthen Sri Lanka’s export performance. Export earnings from Coconut-based Products increased by 3.68 % year-on-year to reach US$ 942.5 Mn during the period of January – September 2026, supported by Fibre-based Products (7.42%), and Shell-based Products (45.91%). The strong performance was driven by increased exports of products such as Coconut Husk Chips (334.15%) and Activated Carbon (37.79%), reflecting sustained global demand and enhanced value addition within the sector. The Rubber and Rubber-based Products sector generated export earnings of US$ 773.88 Mn during January–September 2026, recording an 8.44% year-on-year growth. The positive performance was primarily supported by increased exports of Pneumatic and Retreaded Rubber Tyres and Tubes and Industrial and Surgical Gloves, which grew by 7.67% and 7.58%, respectively. Exports of Gaskets, Washers and Seals also recorded strong growth of 27.78%. This performance reflects the resilience and competitiveness of Sri Lanka’s rubber-based manufacturing sector and its continued presence in global markets. Export earnings from the Food and Beverages sector increased by 20.90% year-on-year, reaching US$ 526.31 Mn during January–September 2026. This growth was largely driven by Processed Food exports, which recorded a notable 34.19% increase to reach US$ 243.28 Mn. Exports of non-alcoholic beverages also grew by 46.78%, while animal feed exports increased by 13.69%. These results highlight the growing export potential of Sri Lanka’s value-added food products and the sector’s contribution to overall export performance. Meanwhile, export earnings from Spices, Essential Oils and Oleoresins increased by 30.53%, reaching US$ 430.53 Mn during January–September 2026. This growth was primarily driven by Pepper and Cinnamon, which recorded year-on-year increases of 61.45% and 31.03%, reaching US$ 136.26 Mn and US$ 221.56 Mn, respectively. Exports of Essential Oils and Oleoresins also increased by 22.17% and 30.09%, respectively. The strong performance of these key products reflects continued international demand for Sri Lanka’s spices and their contribution to export growth. Exports of Electrical & Electronic Components recorded exceptional growth during January–September 2026, increasing by 61.05% year-on-year to reach US$ 508.86 Mn. This performance was supported by significant growth in exports of Insulated Wires and Cables (82.59%), Switches, Boards and Panels (31.49%), and Electrical Transformers (33.46%). Exports of Telephone Sets and Audio/Video Equipment and Parts increased by 234.82%, while Boilers, Piston Engines, Pumps and Vacuum Pumps recorded growth of 508.71%. These results highlight the growing competitiveness and export potential of Sri Lanka’s electrical and electronic manufacturing sector. Furthermore, ICT/BPM exports are estimated to have increased by 3.69% year-on-year, reaching US$ 1,240.67 Mn during January–September 2026, compared with US$ 1,196.55 Mn in the corresponding period of 2025. This growth highlights the continued expansion of Sri Lanka’s digital and knowledge-based economy and the sector’s growing contribution to national export earnings, reinforcing its importance as a high-value, services-oriented export sector. Products with Negative Growth (Decreases) Export earnings from the Apparel and Textiles sector declined by 5.68% year-on-year to US$ 3,783.76 Mn during January–September 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025. The decline was driven by a 5.36% decrease in apparel exports to US$ 3,513.37 Mn and a 9.66% reduction in textile exports to US$ 270.39 Mn. The sector’s performance was affected by subdued demand in key export markets, particularly the United States and the European Union, which together account for more than half of Sri Lanka’s apparel exports. During the period, exports to the United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom declined by 3.83%, 5.54%, and 10.41%, respectively, contributing to the overall contraction amid challenging global market conditions. Tea export earnings declined by 6.83% year-on-year to US$ 1,083.58 Mn during January–September 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025. The decline was mainly driven by lower earnings from Tea Packets and Bulk Tea, which decreased by 4.42% and 11.13%, respectively. Although exports of Tea Bags and Instant Tea grew by 53.39% and 9.85%, respectively, these increases were insufficient to offset the overall decline. The contraction was further influenced by weaker performance in key export markets, particularly the Middle East, where tea exports fell by 34.22%. Within the region, exports to the United Arab Emirates, Iran, and Iraq declined by 59.66%, 65.80%, and 47.72%, respectively, highlighting the challenges facing Sri Lanka’s tea export sector in these markets. Seafood exports declined by 2.03% year-on-year, generating export earnings of US$ 180.81 Mn during January–September 2026. The contraction was mainly associated with lower exports of Frozen Fish, which declined by 1.88%, and Fresh or Chilled Fish, which decreased by 9.59%. Ornamental Fish exports also fell by 26.71%. Table 1: Comparison of Product-wise Merchandise Export Performance Sri Lanka’s Export Performance in Major Markets Among the top fifteen export destinations, several key markets, including United States, India, Italy, China, Turkey, Australia, Belgium, Mexico and Japan, recorded positive year-on-year growth both in September 2026 and cumulatively during January-September 2026. This positive performance across multiple key markets reflects sustained export growth and strengthening demand across these destinations. The United States, Sri Lanka’s largest single export destination, accounting for approximately 20.3% of total merchandise exports, recorded strong year-on-year growth of 18.06% in September 2026, with export earnings reaching US$ 281.84 Mn. Cumulative exports to the United States during January-September 2026 also recorded a marginal increase of 0.05%, reaching US$ 2,252.99 Mn compared with the corresponding period in 2025. This performance reinforces the continued importance of the US market to Sri Lanka’s merchandise exports, maintaining its position as the country’s leading export destination. India strengthened its position as Sri Lanka’s second-largest export destination, surpassing the United Kingdom, with cumulative exports increasing by 12.3% to US$ 889.84 Mn during January-September 2026. Exports to India also recorded robust year-on-year growth of 29.65% in September 2026, reaching US$ 113.22 Mn. In contrast, exports to the United Kingdom declined by 3.17% year-on-year to US$ 71.71 Mn in September 2026, while cumulative exports during January-September 2026 decreased by 9.33% to US$ 654.36 Mn. These trends highlight India’s growing importance as a key destination for Sri Lanka’s merchandise exports, alongside the continued significance of the UK market. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) recorded a 17.8% year-on-year decline in export earnings in September 2026, amounting to US$ 33.66 Mn. Cumulative exports to the UAE during January-September 2026 also declined by 10.5% compared with the corresponding period in 2025, reaching US$ 232.06 Mn. Despite this contraction, the UAE remained an important destination for Sri Lanka’s merchandise exports, highlighting its continued relevance in the country’s export market portfolio. Turkey recorded strong export growth of 64.22% in September 2026, with export earnings reaching US$ 30.71 Mn. Cumulative exports during January–September 2026 also increased substantially by 94.01% year-on-year, reaching US$ 218.24 Mn. This strong performance reflects improved market penetration, and growing demand for Sri Lankan products in the Turkey. Notably, tea exports to Turkey recorded strong year-on-year growth of 82.48% in September 2026, while cumulative tea exports during January–September 2026 increased by 126.51% compared with the corresponding period in 2025. This substantial growth highlights the expanding market for Sri Lankan tea in Turkey and presents opportunities to further strengthen market presence and expand export earnings. China also recorded strong export growth of 9.36% in September 2026, with export earnings reaching US$ 25.48 Mn. Cumulative exports to China during January–September 2026 also increased substantially by 16.46% year-on-year, reaching US$ 234.39 Mn. The strong performance was supported by notable growth in key export products, particularly activated carbon, which recorded year-on-year increases of 55.56% in September 2026 and 78.33% during January–September 2026, compared with the corresponding periods in 2025. Table 2 shows a comparative analysis of merchandise export performance across the top 15 export markets for September 2025 & 2026, along with the cumulative figures for the January- September period of 2025 & 2026. Table 2: Comparison of Merchandise Export Performance of Top 15 Export Destinations Exports to FTA Partners (India & Pakistan) September 2026 Exports to India and Pakistan collectively accounted for 9.04% of Sri Lanka’s total merchandise exports in September 2026, with combined export earnings reaching US$ 125.14 Mn, reflecting a 33.85% year-on-year increase. Exports to India grew by 29.65% to US$ 113.22 Mn, primarily driven by increased exports of pepper. Meanwhile, exports to Pakistan recorded a substantial year-on-year increase of 93.51%, reaching US$ 11.92 Mn. These gains highlight the positive export performance across both South Asian markets during the month. January – September 2026 During January–September 2026, export earnings to India increased by 12.3% year-on-year, reaching US$ 889.84 Mn. This growth was primarily driven by increased exports of pepper, boilers, piston engines, pumps and vacuum pumps, coconut shell charcoal, animal feed, and base metal products. Exports to Pakistan also recorded strong year-on-year growth of 33.59%, reaching US$ 74.73 Mn during the period. This performance was supported by increased exports of other textile articles, desiccated coconut, tea, and other articles of stone, highlighting the growing opportunities for Sri Lankan products in the Pakistani market. Sri Lanka’s Export Performance in Regions Table 3 shows the comparison of region wise exports for September 2025 & 2026, along with the cumulative figures for the January–September period of 2025 & 2026. Table 3: Comparison of Region wise Merchandise Export Performance Exports to the European Union (EU), which accounted for approximately 20.12% of Sri Lanka’s total merchandise exports, recorded a modest year-on-year increase of 1.92% in September 2026 compared with the corresponding month in 2025. However, cumulative exports to the EU during January-September 2026 recorded a marginal decline of 0.15% year-on-year. These relatively modest changes indicate a broadly stable export performance in the EU market, with monthly growth partially offset by the slight contraction in cumulative export earnings. Among the top five EU export markets, Italy remained the leading destination, with export earnings reaching US$ 514.28 Mn, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 1.48% during January–September 2026. Exports to Germany amounted to US$ 513.08 Mn, recording a decline of 4.27%, while exports to the Netherlands decreased by 5.35% to US$ 328.12 Mn. Exports to France also declined by 6.54%, reaching US$ 198.77 Mn. In contrast, exports to Belgium increased by 3.16% to US$ 193.42 Mn during the same period, reflecting varied export performance across the major EU markets. Sources: Data were obtained from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) and Sri Lanka Customs. Export figures of Services, Gems & Jewellery, and Petroleum Products for September 2026 were estimated by the EDB.

content: Sri Lanka’s total exports have reached US$ 13.61 Bn during the first nine months of 2026, recording a year-on-year growth of 5.04% compared with US$ 12.96 Bn in the corresponding period of 2025. This positive performance reflects the continued expansion of the country’s export sector, supported by growth in both merchandise and services exports. According to the latest export performance figures released by Sri Lanka Customs, together with the EDB’s estimates for gems and jewellery and petroleum products, merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$ 10.76 Bn during January–September 2026, compared with US$ 10.22 Bn recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Meanwhile, services exports grew by 3.88% to US$ 2.85 Bn, up from US$ 2.74 Bn in the corresponding period of the previous year. The performance of both segments highlights the importance of strengthening Sri Lanka’s export competitiveness while diversifying its sources of export earnings. Strong Export Performance in September 2026 Sri Lanka recorded a particularly strong performance in September 2026, with total exports reaching US$ 1.69 Bn, an impressive year-on-year increase of 17.23% compared with US$ 1.44 Bn in September 2025. Merchandise exports were the main driver of this monthly growth, increasing by 21.66% to US$ 1.39 Bn, compared with US$ 1.14 Bn in September 2025. Services exports also recorded a positive performance, rising by 0.67% to US$ 306.17 Mn from US$ 304.14 Mn in the corresponding month last year. The strong growth in merchandise exports during September contributed significantly to the overall improvement in export earnings, reinforcing the positive trajectory of Sri Lanka’s export sector. Sustaining Export Growth Towards National Targets The export performance achieved during the first nine months of 2026 represents continued progress towards strengthening Sri Lanka’s position in international markets and expanding its contribution to the national economy. Sustaining this momentum will require continued efforts to diversify export products and markets, enhance value addition, improve product quality and standards, and strengthen the competitiveness of Sri Lankan exporters. The National Export Development Plan (NEDP) 2026–2030, which targets US$ 36 Bn in annual export earnings by 2030, provides a strategic framework for accelerating export growth through improved trade facilitation, market development, investment promotion, innovation, and enhanced private-sector engagement. Building on the positive results recorded in the first nine months of 2026, continued coordination among government institutions, industry stakeholders, and exporters will be essential to maintaining growth, addressing emerging challenges, and realising Sri Lanka’s long-term export development ambitions. Commenting on the export performance in September 2026, Mr.Mangala Wijesinghe, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB), stated: “Sri Lanka’s total exports reaching US$ 13.61 Bn during the first nine months of 2026, representing a growth of 5.04% compared with the corresponding period of 2025, reflects the continued resilience and progress of our export sector. Particularly encouraging is the strong performance recorded in September, when total exports increased by 17.23% year-on-year to US$ 1.69 Bn, driven by a significant 21.66% growth in merchandise exports. This performance demonstrates the potential of Sri Lankan exporters to strengthen their presence in international markets despite an increasingly competitive global trading environment. As we move forward, our priority must be to sustain this growth momentum by strengthening the competitiveness of existing export sectors while accelerating the development of new products, services and markets. Enhancing value addition, promoting innovation and technology adoption, diversifying export markets, and integrating more deeply into global value chains will be essential to expanding export earnings and generating greater economic value for the country. The EDB remains committed to working closely with exporters, industry associations and relevant government institutions to address emerging challenges, improve the trade and investment environment, and facilitate greater access to international markets. Through the effective implementation of the National Export Development Plan 2026–2030 and strengthened collaboration among all stakeholders, we aim to build on these positive results, achieve sustainable export growth, and advance Sri Lanka towards its long-term ambition of reaching US$ 36 Bn in annual export earnings by 2030.”

headline_en: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
summary_en: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
content:
Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US.

The firm's valuation is expected to exceed that of SpaceX, which was the biggest-ever listing at an initial valuation of about $1.8 trillion in the summer.

Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, their price range, or a date for the listing.

The Claude chatbot developer reported $16.3bn (£12.2bn) of revenue in the first half of the year, with losses of more than $80.7bn.

Anthropic, which said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology.

In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said concerns had been raised by policymakers, regulators and researchers as well as by people within its organisation that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity.

It said advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy".

Anthropic was founded five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei and five others, and announced its intention to go public in June.

Its main rival, OpenAI, quickly followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year, according to a person familiar with OpenAI's plans.

Those announcements were followed by a wave of cyber-security and other technological breaches involving their AI agents - bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously.

Current and former staff of both companies also warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI tools.

As Anthropic revealed its stock debut plans on Monday, the owners of the rights to Elvis Presley's music sued the AI firm accusing it of using hundreds of the rock-and-roll star's songs to train its chatbot Claude.

In Anthropic's new documents, it reiterated promises it has made in the past to develop AI in a way that is beneficial to people, while at the same time warning investors of its dangers.

Anthropic detailed losses in its financial filings that exceeded its revenue for the first half of the year, but said it would often make forward investments "that may seem irresponsibly large at first glance".

"In general, we will aim to be bold but sane, and to win trust with a track record of successful bets," the tech giant said.

Its success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, Anthropic said, adding, "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".

Across about 90 pages detailing possible risk factors, Anthropic set out the potential threats to its ability to safely and competitively develop AI.

Anthropic warned it relies on a cluster of cloud computing providers, Taiwanese chipmakers already facing huge demand and data centres concentrated in the US.

It also warned of "regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models" - citing concerns over AI being used by children or individuals at risk of suicide - and uncertainty about where and how it might be held liable for actions taken by its systems.

However, Anthropic also used the filing to laud the potential benefits of the tech itself, envisioning it unlocking "millions of virtual agents with the ability to revolutionise every area of human endeavour" across a range of fields.

Anthropic said AI would also "profoundly accelerate the rate of progress in biology and medicine", potentially finding cures to diseases including cancer and Alzheimer's.

The firm added it could also establish "sustained acceleration in economic growth" by boosting productivity.

Matt Orton, chief market strategist at investment management firm Raymond James Investment, said investors expected to see rapid growth as well as rapid financial losses in Anthropic's finances, so Monday's filing would not come as a surprise.

"Getting the details from this filing, I think will help provide the market with more visibility, because we need to know where its revenue growth is coming from," he told the BBC.

Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital Management, told Reuters that Anthropic's plans to list was "a significant milestone in the development of artificial intelligence".

He added that the outcome of its stock market debut would be "fairly indicative of the sentiment" among investors to continue ploughing cash into AI development.

MAGNATE යනු මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ නවෝත්පාදනය , නායකත්වය සහ දැනුම් හුවමාරුව ප්‍රවර්ධනය කිරීමේ අරමුණින්, මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ ශිෂ්‍ය ශිෂ්‍යාවන්, විද්වතුන්, වෘත්තිකයන් සහ ආයතන ප්‍රධානීන් එකිනෙකා සමඟ සම්බන්ධ කරන වේදිකාවකි. එහි මෙවර අදියරට ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ විශේෂඥයකු විසින් පවත්වන ලද ප්‍රධාන දේශනයක්, සංවාදමය වැඩසටහන් මාලාවක් සහ අන්තර් විශ්වවිද්‍යාල විවාද තරගයක් ඇතුළත් විය. මේ තුළින් සිසුන්ට අදහස් හා දැනුම හුවමාරු කර ගැනීමටත්, මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රය පිළිබඳව වඩාත් පැහැදිලි අවබෝධයක් ලබා ගැනීමටත්, ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ සිදුවෙමින් පවතින වෙනස්කම් සමීපව ගවේෂණය කිරීමටත් අවස්ථාව සැලසිණි. මෙම අවස්ථාවට First Capital Holdings නියෝජනය කරමින් සහභාගී වූ එහි වත්කම් කළමනාකරණ අංශයේ උප සභාපති කුමාරවරන් කනගසූරියර් මහතා “Barter to Bitcoin: Global Shift in Finance Beyond Borders” යන තේමාව යටතේ වැඩසටහනේ ප්‍රධාන දේශනය පැවැත්වූ අතර , එහිදී ඔහු මූල්‍ය පද්ධතිවල විකාශනය සහ වඩාත් අන්තර්සම්බන්ධිත වෙමින් පවතින ගෝලීය මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රය හැඩගස්වන බලවේග පිළිබඳව අදහස් දැක්වීය. මෙම වැඩසටහන සඳහා First Capital දිගින් දිගටම අනුග්‍රාහකත්වය ලබා දීම පිළිබඳව එහි මානව සම්පත් ප්‍රධානී චාමර පුස්සැල්ල මහතා මෙසේ අදහස් පළ කළේය: “අනාගතයේ දක්ෂ වෘත්තිකයන් බවට පත්වීමට නියමිත තරුණ තරුණියන් සමඟ අර්ථවත් සබඳතා ගොඩනංවා ගැනීමේ උත්සාහය තුළ දී, විශ්වවිද්‍යාල ක්ෂේත්‍රය සමඟ එක්ව කටයුතු කිරීම අතිශයින් වැදගත්. MAGNATE වැනි වැඩසටහන් තුළින් මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ අනාගත වෘත්තිකයන් සමඟ සම්බන්ධ වීමටත්, අදහස් හුවමාරු කරගැනීමටත්, ක්ෂේත්‍රය පිළිබඳ වඩාත් හොඳ අවබෝධයක් ඔවුන් වෙත ලබා දීමටත් අපට හැකි වෙනවා. සේවායෝජකයෙකු ලෙස, අධ්‍යාපන ක්ෂේත්‍රය සමඟ සබඳතා අඛණ්ඩව ශක්තිමත් කරගනිමින්, තරුණ දක්ෂයන්ට ඉගෙනීමටත්, වර්ධනය වීමටත්, තමන් සතු හැකියාවන් ගවේෂණය කිරීමටත් අවස්ථා සලසා දීම අපගේ අරමුණයි.” මෙම වැඩසටහනට සම්බන්ධ වීම තුළින් අනාගත සීමාවාසික පුහුණු අවස්ථා පිරිනැමීම සඳහා සුදුසු දක්ෂ තරුණ තරුණියන් හඳුනාගැනීමටද First Capital සමාගමට අවස්ථාව සැලසේ. MAGNATE වැඩසටහනට අඛණ්ඩව සහභාගී වීම තුළින්, සේවායෝජකයෙකු ලෙස කොළඹ විශ්වවිද්‍යාලයේ කළමනාකරණ හා මූල්‍ය පීඨය සමඟ පවතින සබඳතා ශක්තිමත් කිරීමට මෙන්ම, දැනුම හුවමාරු කරගැනීම, මූල්‍ය නවෝත්පාදනය ප්‍රවර්ධනය කිරීම සහ අධ්‍යාපන ක්ෂේත්‍රය හා මූල්‍ය සේවා ක්ෂේත්‍රය අතර වඩාත් සමීප සබඳතා ඇති කිරීම සඳහා දායක වීමට First Capital සමාගම අපේක්ෂා කරයි. ඡායාරූපය: අඛණ්ඩව සිව්වන වසරටත් MAGNATE හි නිල ප්‍රධාන අනුග්‍රාහකයා ලෙස කටයුතු කළ First Capital Holdings PLC සමාගමේ වත්කම් කළමනාකරණ අංශයේ උප සභාපති කුමාරවරන් කනගසූරියර් මහතා එහි ප්‍රධාන දේශනය සිදු කරමින් The post First Capital අඛණ්ඩව සිව්වන වරටත් MAGNATE හි නිල ප්‍රධාන අනුග්‍රාහකයා ලෙස කටයුතු කරයි appeared first on Adaderana Biz Sinhala | Sri Lanka Business News .
passive_voice_content: JXG (ජනශක්ති සමූහ ව්‍යාපාරය) හි අනුබද්ධ සමාගමක් මෙන්ම ශ්‍රී ලංකාවේ ප්‍රාග්ධන වෙළෙඳපොළ ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ පුරෝගාමී බලවේගයක් වන First Capital Holdings PLC, කොළඹ විශ්වවිද්‍යාලයේ කළමනාකරණ හා මූල්‍ය පීඨයේ මූල්‍ය ශිෂ්‍ය සංගමය විසින් සංවිධානය කරන ලද MAGNATE 2026 හි නිල ප්‍රධාන හවුල්කරු ලෙස අඛණ්ඩව සිව්වන වසරටත් එක් විය. අධ්‍යාපන ආයතන සහ මූල්‍ය සේවා ක්ෂේත්‍රය අතර සම්බන්ධතා ශක්තිමත් කරන අතරම දක්ෂ තරුණ තරුණියන් හඳුනා ගනිමින් ඔවුන්ගේ අනාගත වෘත්තීය ජීවිතයට අත්වැලක් වීමේ අරමුණින් First Capital සමාගම මෙම වැඩසටහනට අනුග්‍රාහකත්වය ලබා දෙයි. MAGNATE යනු මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ නවෝත්පාදනය , නායකත්වය සහ දැනුම් හුවමාරුව ප්‍රවර්ධනය කිරීමේ අරමුණින්, මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ ශිෂ්‍ය ශිෂ්‍යාවන්, විද්වතුන්, වෘත්තිකයන් සහ ආයතන ප්‍රධානීන් එකිනෙකා සමඟ සම්බන්ධ කරන වේදිකාවකි. එහි මෙවර අදියරට ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ විශේෂඥයකු විසින් පවත්වන ලද ප්‍රධාන දේශනයක්, සංවාදමය වැඩසටහන් මාලාවක් සහ අන්තර් විශ්වවිද්‍යාල විවාද තරගයක් ඇතුළත් විය. මේ තුළින් සිසුන්ට අදහස් හා දැනුම හුවමාරු කර ගැනීමටත්, මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රය පිළිබඳව වඩාත් පැහැදිලි අවබෝධයක් ලබා ගැනීමටත්, ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ සිදුවෙමින් පවතින වෙනස්කම් සමීපව ගවේෂණය කිරීමටත් අවස්ථාව සැලසිණි. මෙම අවස්ථාවට First Capital Holdings නියෝජනය කරමින් සහභාගී වූ එහි වත්කම් කළමනාකරණ අංශයේ උප සභාපති කුමාරවරන් කනගසූරියර් මහතා “Barter to Bitcoin: Global Shift in Finance Beyond Borders” යන තේමාව යටතේ වැඩසටහනේ ප්‍රධාන දේශනය පැවැත්වූ අතර , එහිදී ඔහු මූල්‍ය පද්ධතිවල විකාශනය සහ වඩාත් අන්තර්සම්බන්ධිත වෙමින් පවතින ගෝලීය මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රය හැඩගස්වන බලවේග පිළිබඳව අදහස් දැක්වීය. මෙම වැඩසටහන සඳහා First Capital දිගින් දිගටම අනුග්‍රාහකත්වය ලබා දීම පිළිබඳව එහි මානව සම්පත් ප්‍රධානී චාමර පුස්සැල්ල මහතා මෙසේ අදහස් පළ කළේය: “අනාගතයේ දක්ෂ වෘත්තිකයන් බවට පත්වීමට නියමිත තරුණ තරුණියන් සමඟ අර්ථවත් සබඳතා ගොඩනංවා ගැනීමේ උත්සාහය තුළ දී, විශ්වවිද්‍යාල ක්ෂේත්‍රය සමඟ එක්ව කටයුතු කිරීම අතිශයින් වැදගත්. MAGNATE වැනි වැඩසටහන් තුළින් මූල්‍ය ක්ෂේත්‍රයේ අනාගත වෘත්තිකයන් සමඟ සම්බන්ධ වීමටත්, අදහස් හුවමාරු කරගැනීමටත්, ක්ෂේත්‍රය පිළිබඳ වඩාත් හොඳ අවබෝධයක් ඔවුන් වෙත ලබා දීමටත් අපට හැකි වෙනවා. සේවායෝජකයෙකු ලෙස, අධ්‍යාපන ක්ෂේත්‍රය සමඟ සබඳතා අඛණ්ඩව ශක්තිමත් කරගනිමින්, තරුණ දක්ෂයන්ට ඉගෙනීමටත්, වර්ධනය වීමටත්, තමන් සතු හැකියාවන් ගවේෂණය කිරීමටත් අවස්ථා සලසා දීම අපගේ අරමුණයි.” මෙම වැඩසටහනට සම්බන්ධ වීම තුළින් අනාගත සීමාවාසික පුහුණු අවස්ථා පිරිනැමීම සඳහා සුදුසු දක්ෂ තරුණ තරුණියන් හඳුනාගැනීමටද First Capital සමාගමට අවස්ථාව සැලසේ. MAGNATE වැඩසටහනට අඛණ්ඩව සහභාගී වීම තුළින්, සේවායෝජකයෙකු ලෙස කොළඹ විශ්වවිද්‍යාලයේ කළමනාකරණ හා මූල්‍ය පීඨය සමඟ පවතින සබඳතා ශක්තිමත් කිරීමට මෙන්ම, දැනුම හුවමාරු කරගැනීම, මූල්‍ය නවෝත්පාදනය ප්‍රවර්ධනය කිරීම සහ අධ්‍යාපන ක්ෂේත්‍රය හා මූල්‍ය සේවා ක්ෂේත්‍රය අතර වඩාත් සමීප සබඳතා ඇති කිරීම සඳහා දායක වීමට First Capital සමාගම අපේක්ෂා කරයි. ඡායාරූපය: අඛණ්ඩව සිව්වන වසරටත් MAGNATE හි නිල ප්‍රධාන අනුග්‍රාහකයා ලෙස කටයුතු කළ First Capital Holdings PLC සමාගමේ වත්කම් කළමනාකරණ අංශයේ උප සභාපති කුමාරවරන් කනගසූරියර් මහතා එහි ප්‍රධාන දේශනය සිදු කරමින් The post First Capital අඛණ්ඩව සිව්වන වරටත් MAGNATE හි නිල ප්‍රධාන අනුග්‍රාහකයා ලෙස කටයුතු කරයි appeared first on Adaderana Biz Sinhala | Sri Lanka Business News .

content: An eight-member team from Ceylinco Life recently participated in a four-day leadership training programme in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, designed to strengthen agency management capabilities and equip the company’s sales leaders with practical strategies to enhance branch performance. Conducted under the theme ‘Lead Forward, Build.’ the programme covered key areas including digital engagement for insurance professionals, performance management, leadership enhancement and development, and the creation of office environments that support and drive sales. The training was facilitated by five accomplished Group Sales Managers from Great Eastern Life Insurance in Malaysia and Singapore, led by industry veteran Mr. K. Haridas. Combining knowledge-sharing with practical application, the programme challenged participants to address real-life branch management issues through a group exercise in which two teams assessed existing situations, identified root causes and implications, and developed action plans to tackle the challenges more effectively. Participants also gained hands-on experience in creating videos and digital content for social media platforms and developing Agency Management Blueprints to address specific branch-level challenges. The programme provided valuable insights and actionable strategies to strengthen agency leadership, improve branch management and enhance overall performance. Representing Ceylinco Life were one Zonal Manager, four Regional Sales Managers, two Agency Heads and a representative from the company’s Head Office. Pictured here are members of the Ceylinco Life team with Mr. Haridas and representatives of Great Eastern Life Insurance.

headline_en: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
summary_en: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
content:
Rapper Nicki Minaj said US President Donald Trump has "changed the energy of the country" as she joined him at a Michigan rally to stump for Republicans ahead of the nationwide midterm elections.

"He's given us a future to look forward to," she said, after Trump praised her figure and called her on stage to speak.

Minaj has called herself Trump's "number one fan" despite criticising some of his policies in his first term.

In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is locked in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers with just over a week to go before the midterms. Former President Barack Obama held a rally - one of the first in this cycle - with the Democrat on Saturday.

Democrats are also aggressively hitting the campaign trail, with close elections taking place on 3 November which will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency.

In his remarks on Sunday, Trump focused on El-Sayed's Muslim faith and background, alleging that he will "invite jihadists" into America if he wins.

El-Sayed has criticised similar remarks by Trump as Islamophobic, saying in an ad to voters last week that the US president "thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office".

In Port Huron on Sunday, Minaj, wearing a gold-coloured Gucci-branded suit, led the crowd in chanting Trump's name, and the names of Republican candidates in Michigan.

"We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country," she said.

"She never looked more beautiful," Trump said as she left the stage. "She gets it. She's smart," he added.

Earlier in his speech, Trump praised the rear end of one male Republican candidate before turning the crowd's attention to Minaj.

"By the way, I looked at a beautiful ass before," he segued. “Nicki Minaj. That's hard to miss.”

He then asked her to "stand up" as the crowd cheered, and added that he hoped she was not "insulted" by his remark.

The Super Bass singer had accompanied Trump to the state aboard Air Force One. She filmed a video with an aide - which was posted to X -on the president's plane, pretending to be interviewing for the White House press secretary role.

The position is currently open after Katie Zacharia left five days after a shaky public debut.

The Trinidad and Tobago-born rapper has thrown her star power behind Trump a few times before, including on his allegations that Christians face persecution in Nigeria and his "gold card" visa, which offers applicants residency and a path to US citizenship.

content: Samsung Sri Lanka has expanded its easy payment facility through Lesi Pay by Dialog Finance, making convenient monthly instalment options available at approximately 400 authorised Samsung outlets across the country, in addition to Dialog showrooms. The expanded facility aims to reach 1,000 outlets by the end of 2026, improving access to genuine Samsung smartphones and tablets across Sri Lanka. Through Lesi Pay by Dialog Finance, eligible customers can purchase genuine Samsung devices with monthly instalments starting from Rs. 3,657, without requiring a credit card or guarantor, with repayment periods of up to 18 months. Customers purchasing through authorised channels also benefit from Samsung’s official warranty and the Samsung Break-Free offer, available for up to 24 months, subject to applicable terms and conditions. The facility covers selected Samsung smartphones and tablets, including the Galaxy A07, Galaxy F07, Galaxy F06 5G, Galaxy A17 5G, Galaxy M17 5G and Galaxy Tab A11. Offered by Dialog Finance, Lesi Pay is a loan facility designed to help eligible customers spread the cost of selected devices through structured monthly repayments. The facility removes the need for a credit card or guarantor, while allowing customers to check their eligibility through the Dialog Pay app before selecting a device. Loan approval, repayment terms and applicable interest rates are determined by Dialog Finance, subject to eligibility and the relevant terms and conditions. To purchase a device, customers can download the Dialog Pay app, check their eligibility, select an eligible Samsung device and collect it from a participating outlet. The facility is available through participating Dialog showrooms and authorised Samsung retailers, making it more convenient for customers across Sri Lanka to access the service. Commenting on the expansion, Mr. Dongkyun Lee, Managing Director, Samsung Sri Lanka & Maldives, said, “Expanding Dialog Lesi Pay to our authorised retail network is an important step towards making genuine Samsung devices more accessible to customers across Sri Lanka. By offering convenient instalment options through more retail locations, we are giving customers greater flexibility when purchasing their preferred devices, supported by the assurance of Samsung’s official warranty and after-sales services.” Nazeem Mohammed, CEO and Director of Dialog Finance PLC, said, “At Dialog Finance, our focus is on making financing simpler, more accessible, and relevant to the everyday needs of Sri Lankans. Lesi Pay reflects this commitment by enabling customers to own the devices they need through convenient and flexible monthly instalments, without the requirement for a credit card or guarantor. Expanding this facility across Samsung’s authorised retail network is an important step in bringing accessible financing closer to more customers islandwide. Through partnerships such as this, we aim to bridge the gap between financial accessibility and digital connectivity, empowering more Sri Lankans to benefit from technology that supports their daily lives.” For further information, customers can download the Dialog Pay app or visit a participating Dialog showroom or authorised Samsung retailer.

content: TBWA\Sri Lanka has earned multiple international accolades at the 2026 Dragons of Asia Awards in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, demonstrating how disruptive thinking can translate into work that earns recognition beyond its home market. The agency secured the prestigious Blue Dragon for Best Campaign in Sri Lanka and a Gold Dragon in Artificial Intelligence for Hutch Roaming – The Roaming Hack while Maliban HumaniTill won a Bronze Dragon in Event or Experiential Marketing. Adding to the achievement, TBWA\Sri Lanka was ranked among Asia’s Top 10 agencies in The Dragon Elite: Asia. The Blue Dragon recognises the impact of Hutch Roaming – The Roaming Hack in Sri Lanka, while the Gold Dragon acknowledges its innovative application of artificial intelligence. The campaign was also shortlisted for Best Campaign in Asia, placing it among the contenders for regional recognition. The wins reflect the agency’s philosophy of Disruption® in Action: questioning the obvious, challenging the expected and turning real consumer problems into ideas that create value for brands and the audiences. “Disruption® in Action is more than a philosophy; it is how the agency approach the work. It means challenging the expected and finding different ways to solve real problems. To see our work recognised at the Dragons of Asia and to have TBWA\Sri Lanka ranked among Asia’s Top 10 agencies, is a powerful affirmation of what we stand for,” said Renuka Marshall, Managing Director, TBWA\Sri Lanka. Maliban HumaniTill, created for Maliban Biscuit Manufactories, earned a Bronze Dragon in Event or Experiential Marketing, recognising the campaign’s creative execution and its ability to bring the brand closer to its audience through an engaging experience-led approach. This recognition adds to the campaign’s growing list of accolades and reflects another expression of TBWA\Sri Lanka’s commitment to finding unconventional ways for brands to connect with people. Nathasoruban Sivapatham, Chief Creative Officer, TBWA\Sri Lanka, said “Creativity is at its most powerful when it changes how people think. Our role is to look beyond the obvious and find ideas that have a reason to exist in their lives. That means being curious, questioning our first answers and pushing ourselves to create work that is both distinctive and relevant.” The agency’s international success follows a strong performance at the 2026 Dragons of Sri Lanka, where TBWA\Sri Lanka was named No. 1 Industry Leader, winning seven awards across four campaigns. “Disruptive work takes more than bold thinking. It takes clients who are willing to challenge convention, trust new ideas and back a different path. These recognitions celebrate that shared courage, collaboration and the work they make possible,” said Ahmed T. Hassan, Chief Operating Officer, TBWA\Sri Lanka. From applying artificial intelligence in unexpected ways to creating engaging brand experiences, TBWA\Sri Lanka continues to challenge conventional approaches to communications. Its latest wins at the Dragons of Asia demonstrate how bold thinking, strong client partnerships and a willingness to do things differently can create work that resonates beyond borders. content: Former Energy Minister Patali Champika Ranawaka says members of the Presidential Commission of Inquiry into coal-related matters have clearly informed him that he faces no allegations in connection with coal transactions. He made these remarks while speaking to the media today (26) after appearing before the Presidential Commission of Inquiry investigating coal-related matters. Ranawaka said the Commission had given him an opportunity to present facts regarding a statement made by an official of the Ceylon Shipping Corporation, alleging that he had failed to assist in unloading two coal shipments, identified as shipments 16 and 17, which arrived during the rough monsoon season. He stressed that, apart from this matter, no allegations had been levelled against him. He said the issue concerned the fault of those who had arranged for the ships to arrive during the rough monsoon season. Ranawaka further said the Commission wanted to establish more facts based on testimony given by Kanchana Rathwatte, an official of the Ceylon Shipping Corporation, and that he would present further information on the matter in due course. He also said: “A media campaign has been launched to cover up the fraud involving 30 coal shipments under Anura Kumara Dissanayake. We have decided to expose every detail of this fraud without leaving out a single word. This opportunity will arise on the 12th of next month at the Foundation Institute. We will disclose these facts to leading media organisations and everyone interested in this matter.”

content: Ministers and senior security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – the three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement – are in Tehran to discuss regional security issues amid threats of new US strikes on Iran. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani military chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and will discuss tensions with security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The meetings are among the highest-profile dialogues held in Tehran in recent months. While there is still little information on what might be discussed, the meetings come amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to deal with a new escalation between the United States and Iran. But analysts broadly believe the visit to Tehran by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a regional defence alliance, will be enough to prevent a new outbreak in violence between the US and Iran. “The Mecca pact’s 11th-hour visit to Tehran is an attempt to tip the balance in favour of those willing to compromise before the guns start blazing again,” said Ali Vaez, deputy director of the Middle East and North Africa Program at the International Crisis Group. “But unless they arrive with a credible formula to bridge the US-Iran divide, they may find themselves with little more than goodwill in a race against the clock.” (Aljazeera)

summary_en: Dubai plans world's longest 24-karat gold walkway by end of 2026
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Dubai plans world's longest 24-karat gold walkway by end of 2026
content:
Dubai is set to add another attraction to its list of tourist experiences, with plans to open a walkway made of 24-karat gold before the end of 2026.

The Dubai Gold District says the attraction will be the first of its kind and the longest gold walkway in the world, Gulf Today reported. The walkway is expected to open within the next two months, according to Rashid Al Harmoudi, Senior Director of the Commercial Sector at Dubai Gold District.

The project aims to offer visitors a unique experience while strengthening Dubai's position as a global centre for gold trading and tourism.

The announcement comes as Dubai celebrates another milestone involving gold jewellery. A pair of traditional Indian jhumka earrings created by Joyalukkas Jewellery secured two Guinness World Records for the heaviest pair of gold earrings and the largest pair of earrings in the world. Speaking at an event announcing the record for gold earrings, Al Harmoudi said the walkway would allow visitors to experience a golden path within the district.

The proposed walkway is part of Dubai Gold District's broader plans to bring gold trading, jewellery retail and tourism experiences together in one destination. Located in Deira, the district was launched in January 2026 and brings together businesses dealing in gold, jewellery, bullion, wholesale trading and investment.

According to the Dubai Media Office, the district is home to more than 1,000 retailers across categories such as gold, jewellery, perfumery, cosmetics and lifestyle products. The district is also planning a gold and jewellery trade exhibition that aims to become the largest of its kind in the Middle East. Expansion work is underway to provide additional office and retail space for businesses looking to establish a presence there.

Al Harmoudi said the district had recorded 20% growth in the number of wholesale gold trading offices beginning operations since the start of the year. The number of new stores specialising in gold, jewellery, precious stones and luxury watches has also increased by 15%.

He expects the number of companies moving to the district to grow by 10% to 20% over the coming year as expansion plans continue. The gold walkway is expected to add to these efforts by attracting more visitors and further highlighting Dubai's long-standing association with the precious metal.

summary_en: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies aged 46
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies aged 46
content:
Eric Bauza, the voice artist behind Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died aged 46.

A statement from the Emmy award-winning star's family posted on Instagram said he had died "suddenly".

Bauza had voiced a number of characters in this summer's animated hit Coyote vs. Acme, and appeared in the recent release Forgotten Island.

Variety reports that the cause of death was hypertensive cardiovascular disease and that Bauza died at home on Sunday.

In a 2021 interview with NBC News, Bauza, who was born in Ontario and was of Filipino descent, said he grew up a huge fan of the Looney Tunes characters and used to copy the voices as a child.

"Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures," he said. "It doesn't matter what part of the planet you're from. You get the comedy."

He voiced Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Elmer Fudd and Foghorn Leghorn in 2021's Space Jam: A New Legacy before reprising those roles and that of Road Runner in Coyote vs. Acme.

He also played the part of Toad General in 2023's The Super Mario Bros. Movie and its sequel The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, the fifth highest-grossing film internationally this year.

Between 2022 and 2025, he won three Emmy awards for outstanding voice performance in a number of TV series.

In a statement reported by the Hollywood Reporter, Channing Dungey, the chairman of Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, said: "Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world.

“He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life.”

content: The IPL auction for the 2027 season will take place on December 16 in Goa. The day-long mini-auction will be held on the same day as the second ODI between India and Sri Lanka in Bengaluru. The auction will take place nearly a month after the reten deadline, which the IPL recently informed the franchises will be November 15. Soon after that, the IPL will send the franchises the registered pool of players to shortlist from before the final list is sent out, along with the order of the sets, in the week leading into the auction. The IPL trade window has seen just two trades since the 2026 season ended. According to the IPL rules, the trade window starts a month after a season ends, stays open up to a week before the auction date, and then continues up until a month before the start of the next season. In June, Lucknow Super Giants swapped their captain Risbah Pant to Delhi Capitals (DC) in return for wristspinner Kuldeep Yadav. Recently, DC also traded fast bowler T Natarajan to Sunrisers Hyderabad for uncapped legspinner Zeeshan Ansari. The IPL has not yet finalised the dates for the 2027 season. But, in 2024, while announcing the dates for the following three seasons, it had chalked out the window between March 14 and May 30. However, in September this year, post the BCCI’s AGM, board secretary Devajit Saikia had indicated that the tournament could start in March-end. This is the last mini-auction in the IPL’s current cycle, with a mega auction scheduled ahead of the 2028 season. The next mega auction will kick-off the IPL’s next media rights cycle, though the BCCI is yet to release the tender. In 2022, the IPL joined the ivy league of global sport after the media rights were sold for an astronomical sum of INR 48,390.5 crore (US$ 6.2 billion approx.). (Cricinfo)

content: A racecourse has been fined £6,500 after a jockey was taken to hospital in a horsebox instead of an ambulance. The incident took place in March at Sedgefield Racecourse in County Durham. A disciplinary panel of the British Horseracing Authority (BHA) found that the racecourse had failed to comply with five “general instructions” within its Rules of Racing. The injured jockey’s identity was kept private but it was reported that he suffered a left clavicle and shoulder injury after a fall, and was examined by a doctor at the course. He was cleared to race again but said he was still in pain, which resulted in a doctor advising him to go to A&E. By then all the ambulance crews had left the venue, and he was taken in a horsebox with the medical staff following behind. “The ‘general instructions’ require proper transfer to hospital with accompaniment from qualified medical staff not, as here, being followed in a car,” the BHA panel said. It also added that the jockey was in too much pain to get into the following car. The other failings at the venue included a telephone line not working and “tired worn rooms not conveying a clean clinical area”. The racecourse has acknowledged the “errors and shortcomings” and an inspection took place in April which revealed “significant progress”. (BBC)

content: Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos. A stretch of water between Rothschild Island and Alexander Island in the west of the White Continent is now called the Amos Channel. Amos was given the honour for his “exceptional and influential role in bringing Antarctic research to the forefront of public understanding” during his 38-year career at BBC News, the naming committee said. The channel is a new feature in Antarctica that appeared when a chunk of ice that connected Rothschild and Alexander Islands disintegrated. Jonathan Amos reported on science at the BBC for many years (BBC) The melting ice sheets of this remote continent are just one of many aspects of polar science that Amos reported on while at the BBC. He also covered colossal icebergs, the fate of penguin colonies and a BBC exclusive about the discovery of Ernest Shackelton’s lost ship, the Endurance . “It’s absolutely incredible – what an extraordinary accolade. I’m so touched that there’s a little bit of Antarctica named after me,” Amos said. Despite his fascination with the South Pole, he has not yet travelled to the continent. “I’ve written about it so often, but always from my desk – this is quite the incentive to go and visit. “Antarctica is the front line of the biggest news story on planet Earth – climate change,” he added. The naming of geographical features in Antarctica follows strict rules. The Amos Channel was recommended by the UK Antarctic Place Names Committee, which looks after names for sites within the British Antarctic Territory, as well as South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. Athena Dinar, from the British Antarctic Survey, said: “Jon’s passion for Antarctica and engaging journalism offers something for every reader, viewer or listener. “The naming of an Antarctic place in his honour is a fitting recognition of his outstanding contribution to the promotion of Antarctic research.” Amos joined the BBC in 1986 as a local radio reporter in Cambridge. He was part of the team that launched the BBC News website in 1997, and ran the online science desk for many years. He later worked as a BBC science correspondent across TV, radio and online, before leaving the organisation in 2024. “Jon consistently highlighted the importance of Antarctic research, explaining not only what science is being done there, but why it matters for society, climate understanding and the global environment,” said Fiona Fox, from the Science Media Centre. (BBC)

content: Significant rainfall has been recorded in the upper catchment areas of the Kelani River Basin. Based on the prevailing rainfall conditions and the analysis of water levels recorded at the river gauging stations maintained by the Department of Irrigation within the Kelani River Basin, there is a risk of minor flooding occurring within the next 24 hours from now in the low-lying areas of the Kelani River Valley falling within the Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Ruwanwella, Seethawaka, Dompe, Dehiowita, Eheliyagoda, Yatiyantota and Bulathkohupitiya. The public residing in these areas and motorists travelling through these areas are requested to exercise extreme caution in view of this situation. Furthermore, if heavy rainfall continues, there is a possibility that this flood situation may also affect the low-lying areas of the Kelani River Valley downstream of Hanwella. Disaster Management authorities are requested to take necessary precautionary measures in this regard.

content: The IPL auction for the 2027 season will take place on December 16 in Goa. The day-long mini-auction will be held on the same day as the second ODI between India and Sri Lanka in Bengaluru. The auction will take place nearly a month after the reten deadline, which the IPL recently informed the franchises will be November 15. Soon after that, the IPL will send the franchises the registered pool of players to shortlist from before the final list is sent out, along with the order of the sets, in the week leading into the auction. The IPL trade window has seen just two trades since the 2026 season ended. According to the IPL rules, the trade window starts a month after a season ends, stays open up to a week before the auction date, and then continues up until a month before the start of the next season. In June, Lucknow Super Giants swapped their captain Risbah Pant to Delhi Capitals (DC) in return for wristspinner Kuldeep Yadav. Recently, DC also traded fast bowler T Natarajan to Sunrisers Hyderabad for uncapped legspinner Zeeshan Ansari. The IPL has not yet finalised the dates for the 2027 season. But, in 2024, while announcing the dates for the following three seasons, it had chalked out the window between March 14 and May 30. However, in September this year, post the BCCI’s AGM, board secretary Devajit Saikia had indicated that the tournament could start in March-end. This is the last mini-auction in the IPL’s current cycle, with a mega auction scheduled ahead of the 2028 season. The next mega auction will kick-off the IPL’s next media rights cycle, though the BCCI is yet to release the tender. In 2022, the IPL joined the ivy league of global sport after the media rights were sold for an astronomical sum of INR 48,390.5 crore (US$ 6.2 billion approx.). (Cricinfo)

content: The action drama crossed the lifetime global collection of 2.0, starring Rajinikanth and Akshay Kumar, which had earned approximately Rs 691 crore during its theatrical run. On Sunday, October 25, Jailer 2 took its worldwide gross collection to Rs 710.35 crore, according to trade tracker Sacnilk. The film’s latest milestone comes 11 days after its theatrical release on October 15. With this achievement, Jailer 2 has also emerged as the highest-grossing Tamil film of 2026. At the domestic box office, Jailer 2 recorded a gross collection of Rs 25.70 crore on Sunday. Its total India gross now stands at Rs 466.85 crore, while its India nett collection has reached Rs 398.70 crore. According to Sacnilk, the Tamil version contributed Rs 17.35 crore on Day 11 from 5,683 shows. The Telugu version added Rs 4.50 crore across 1,860 shows, while the Hindi version collected Rs 3.15 crore from 4,195 shows. The Kannada version contributed another Rs 0.70 crore from 216 shows. The film’s strong performance across multiple language versions has helped it maintain its box office momentum and achieve the worldwide record. Jailer 2 Sets Multiple Box Office Records Besides overtaking 2.0 to claim the top spot among Tamil films worldwide, Jailer 2 had already registered several milestones during its opening days. The film became the fastest Tamil release to cross the Rs 300 crore and Rs 400 crore marks in worldwide collections, achieving the former within three days and the latter on Day 4. The latest achievement further strengthens Rajinikanth’s position as one of Tamil cinema’s biggest box office draws. Director Nelson Dilipkumar also reacted to the film’s performance in theatres. Celebrating the audience response, he wrote on X, “Theatres are going bonkers! Thalaivar magic hits different. Thank you, dear audience, for the phenomenal love and reception for #Jailer2. Nothing beats seeing the audience celebrate it like this! Thank you all for the love and support. @rajinikanth sir @anirudhofficial @sunpictures.” Background Bankrolled by Sun Pictures, Jailer 2 features a large ensemble cast alongside Rajinikanth. The film stars Ramya Krishnan, Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Jackie Shroff, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa, Rithvik, S. J. Suryah, Vidya Balan, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Mithun Chakraborty, Hrithik Roshan, Vijay Sethupathi, Jatin Sarna, Namo Narayana, Hakkim Shahjahan and Kottayam Nazeer. (NDTV)

content: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. “I am here. With you,” Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital. She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night. “Night of reunion in our Caracas. For the reunion of each family, for the Freedom of each political prisoner, for the Freedom of Venezuela,” she wrote on X. Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: “I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil.” “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country “toward freedom”. An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied. It’s unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she’s back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted. A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election – held outside the Maduro government’s official election authority – in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote. Despite winning the primary, Maduro’s government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize. In the 2024 election, Machado’s ally González ran in her place against Maduro. The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public. The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence. Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty. A spokesman for Machado called her return “a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future”. “We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support,” her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, “I don’t know anything about” her return, and added that he hoped she was “safe”. “I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe,” he said. In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel prize award to Trump . The committee that issues the prize had said “it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others”. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country’s role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks. “The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela is the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile,” he posted on X. He added: “We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy.” BBC The post Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile appeared first on DailyNews .

content: Warning for strong winds and rough seas Issued by the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centreaa Issued at 09.30 a.m. 26 October 2026, valid for the next 12 hours The Deep Depression over the East-central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has intensified into cyclonic storm “Arnab”. It has moved westwards and lay centered at 5.30 a.m. of today, the 26th October, 2026, near Latitude 15.4°N and Longitude 88.9°E. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards, and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over west central Bay of Bengal by 1800 UTC of 26th October and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on 27th October. Wind speeds in the sea areas marked under the “Warning” category may increase to 80-100 kmph at times, heavy thundershowers can occur, the wave height may increase about (3.0 –4.0) meters in the mentioned sea areas and the sea conditions in these areas will become very rough. Therefore, Naval and fishing communities are warned not to venture to the sea areas bounded by 10N to 20N latitude and 80E to 95E longitude until further notice. Naval and fishing communities operating in those sea areas are advised to move away from the affected sea areas.
